recentItems.title: Iran's Basij Commander Killed: Tehran Agencies Allege US-Israel 'Links' To Assassination | WATCH
recentItems.description:
Iran is investigating a deadly attack that killed Afsaneh Aqila, a female Basij unit commander, in Sistan and Baluchestan province. Iranian state media reported she was shot outside her home in Mehrestan. An IRGC-affiliated agency alleged links between the attackers and the US and Israel, but provided no supporting evidence. A separate attack also killed an Iranian security officer, as violence targeting security forces continues to raise concerns across southeastern Iran.

recentItems.description:
A suspected attack plot targeting Hindus has triggered alarm in Illinois after 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis was arrested in connection with an alleged terrorist threat and weapons offences. Police say investigators recovered a rifle, loaded magazines, ammunition and tactical equipment, while a document reportedly contained white supremacist and extremist statements. The FBI is assisting the investigation, and Hindu places of worship have been alerted. Authorities have not confirmed the exact intended target or independently verified every detail reported about the alleged incident.

recentItems.title: Trump’s White House Secretary Zacharia Under Fire Over Legal Credentials After ‘FAILED’ Remark
recentItems.description:
US White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is facing scrutiny over her legal credentials following reports that she failed California’s bar examination after graduating from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011. According to The Wall Street Journal, public records searches did not identify her as a licensed attorney in California, Texas or Washington, DC. During her first White House briefing, Zacharia’s response to a question about where she passed the bar exam further intensified the controversy. She has defended her professional experience, citing work in international transaction law, including at a Beijing-based law firm, while White House Communications Director Steven Cheung defended her appointment. The debate centres on the distinction between holding a law degree, working in international legal roles and being formally licensed to practise law in a particular jurisdiction.

recentItems.title: Iran Targets Starlink! Tehran Calls Musk’s Satellite Network A ‘Tool Of War’ And Vows Crackdown
recentItems.description:
Iran has vowed to intensify its crackdown on Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite internet service, describing it as a “tool of war” that Tehran claims could facilitate surveillance, intelligence gathering and military coordination. Mohammad Amin Aghamiri, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Cyberspace Council, said authorities had developed systems to disrupt Starlink terminals but did not disclose technical details. The crackdown reportedly includes signal jamming, GPS spoofing, surveillance and legal penalties for possessing or distributing terminals, with severe punishments possible in cases involving additional national security charges. Starlink has helped some Iranians share protest footage internationally despite government-imposed internet restrictions. Tehran has also pursued diplomatic action through the International Telecommunication Union, as internet access remains a major point of contention amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

recentItems.title: Istanbul Floods Turn Deadly: Heavy Rains Trigger Landslides, Flight Diverted; Schools Shut As 2 Die
recentItems.description:
Istanbul is reeling under deadly floods after torrential rains triggered landslides, submerged roads and disrupted air travel. At least two people have died as floodwaters inundated homes, businesses, hospitals and metro stations. Dozens of flights were diverted at Istanbul Airport, while severe traffic congestion brought the city to a standstill. Authorities deployed thousands of personnel for rescue and relief operations. Schools were shut across several regions as officials urged residents to avoid flooded roads and vulnerable areas.
